To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the TMR water vapor path delay measurements have an instrument-related downward bias of approximately 1.5 mm/year over the first four years of the TOPE X mission and that there is no evidence for a significant scale error in the path delay measurements.

the TOPEX microwave radiometers (TMR) measurements of the atmospheric path delays due to water vapor are accurate and stable, with the exception of a 1.0 to 1.5 mm yr drift that was present in the path delays from October 1992 through December 1996.

the TMR water vapor radiometer has performed well over its first five years, with no significant scale error, a small but possibly non-negligible bias of <10mm, and a 1.0 to 1.5 mm/year instrument-related path delay drift from October 1992 through December 1996.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the accuracy of the TOPOEX Microwave Radiometer ( TMR) measurement of atmospheric water vapor.
the stability and accuracy of TMR path delay measurement over a six-year period.
the evaluation of the performance of the TOPEXT Microwave Radiometer (TM) over the first six years of the TOPEXI mission.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TMR water vapor path delay measurements are stable to within 10 mm and accurate to within 2% over the 1992-98 time span.
TMR has been performing well in terms of both stability and accuracy over its first six years.
the TMR has been a stable and reliable measurement of atmospheric water vapor path delay over its first six years of operation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TMR water vapor path delay measurements are stable, accurate, and useful to within a few millimeters over the 6-year interval.
the TMR data are accurate and stable, but that the TMR instrument is drifting.
the TMR instrument has performed as designed over the past six years, and that the TMR data are useful for studies of global water vapor variability and trends.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TMR water vapor path delays can be used with confidence for the 1992-96 time period and with some confidence for the 6-year period 1992-98.
the TMR data have provided a stable and accurate measure of the path delay due to atmospheric water vapor over the entire mission.
the TMR data set is of sufficient quality and accuracy for use in the determination of ocean topography and sea level change, provided that the TMR instrument-related drifts are accounted for.
